title: What Is the Average NBL Salary? Hourly to Annual Conversion with Casual Loading and Super
description: Learn how to convert your hourly rate to annual salary using the 38-hour week. Understand casual loading, super paid on top, and how the average NBL salary compares to official ABS
salarySummary: For a full-time employee on the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, the annual gross salary is $52,254.80 based on 38 hours per week for 52 weeks.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect my annual salary?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an additional 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for lack of paid leave. For example, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour becomes $33.05 per hour with casual loading. When converting to an annual salary, multiply the loaded rate by hours per week and 52. However, casual employees do not accrue annual or sick leave, so the higher hourly rate reflects that.

faqs.q: Is superannuation included in my salary or paid on top?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of your gross salary. The Super Guarantee requires employers to contribute 12% of your ordinary time earnings into a super fund, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. This means your total remuneration package is higher than your annual salary figure. For example, on a $52,254.80 annual salary, the super contribution would be an additional $6,270.58, bringing total package to $58,525.38.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage ($26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026) applies to employees not covered by an award or agreement. Most employees are covered by a modern award that sets higher minimum rates for specific industries or occupations. Award rates can include penalty rates, overtime, and allowances. Always check your award via the Fair Work Ombudsman's Pay and Conditions Tool to ensure you are receiving the correct minimum pay.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Your Hourly Rate to an Annual Salary

When you know your hourly rate, the simplest way to estimate your annual gross salary is to multiply that rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. This article assumes a standard full-time week of 38 hours, as defined by the Fair Work Commission for the National Minimum Wage. If your hours differ, adjust accordingly.

For example, an employee earning the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour would have an annual salary of:

$26.44 × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $52,254.80

This figure is gross pay before tax and super. The same formula applies to any hourly rate, including award rates or above-award wages.

### The Average NBL Salary and Official Benchmarks

You may have heard of the "average NBL salary" from industry surveys or recruiter reports. When evaluating such figures, it is important to compare them against official data from the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS). The ABS Average Weekly Earnings report for May 2026 shows full-time adult ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 per week, which equates to an annual salary of approximately $108,352.40 (based on 52 weeks). For all employees including part-time, total earnings average $1,579.20 per week, or about $82,118.40 annually. These official figures provide a reliable benchmark for the average NBL salary or any other industry average.

If a recruiter survey claims a different average NBL salary, cross-check it with the ABS data. The Fair Work Ombudsman and Fair Work Commission are also authoritative sources for minimum pay rates.

## Casual Loading and Its Impact on Annual Pay

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of their base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave entitlements such as annual leave or sick leave. This loading is clearly defined in the National Minimum Wage Order and many modern awards.

For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $26.44 × 1.25 = $33.05 per hour. If you are a casual employee, your annual salary calculation should use this loaded rate:

$33.05 × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $65,302.80

However, remember that this higher annual figure does not include paid leave. When comparing job offers, consider the total value of permanent employment (including leave) versus casual employment (higher hourly rate but no paid leave).

### Fortnightly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, simply double your weekly pay. For a permanent full-time employee on the National Minimum Wage:

Weekly: $1,004.90
Fortnightly: $2,009.80

For a casual employee on the loaded rate:

Weekly: $1,255.90
Fortnightly: $2,511.80

## Superannuation Is Paid on Top

Superannuation Guarantee contributions are not deducted from your salary; they are paid by your employer on top of your gross earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year.

Using the National Minimum Wage example:

Annual salary: $52,254.80
Super contribution (12%): $6,270.58
Total remuneration package: $58,525.38

For a casual employee on the loaded rate:

Annual salary: $65,302.80
Super contribution (12%): $7,836.34
Total package: $73,139.14

Super is not included in the annual salary figure shown on your pay slip or employment contract. It is an additional benefit that boosts your retirement savings.

## Distinguishing Between Pay Types

- **National Minimum Wage**: $26.44 per hour for adult employees not covered by an award or agreement. [Learn more about the minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage).
- **Award Rates**: Most employees are covered by a modern award that sets higher minimum rates. Award rates vary by industry and classification.
- **Casual Loading**: An extra 25% on top of the base rate for casual employees. See our [casual loading guide](/topics/casual-loading) for details.
- **Annualised Wages**: Some awards allow employers to pay a fixed annual amount that covers base pay, penalties, overtime, and allowances. The Fair Work Ombudsman requires annualised wage arrangements to be reviewed each year to ensure the employee is not worse off.

## Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your annual gross salary is not what you take home. The Australian Taxation Office (ATO) applies progressive tax rates for 2026–27:

- Nil on income up to $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (with possible reductions for low-income earners).

For the National Minimum Wage annual salary of $52,254.80, the estimated tax (including Medicare) would be approximately $7,717, leaving a take-home pay of about $44,538 per year. Use our [take-home pay calculator](/topics/take-home) for a personalised estimate.

## Summary

Converting an hourly rate to an annual salary is straightforward: multiply by hours per week and 52. Always specify whether you are using a base rate or a casual-loaded rate. Super is paid on top. When evaluating the average NBL salary, rely on official ABS data and Fair Work Commission rates rather than unverified surveys. For more tools, see our [hourly conversion guide](/topics/hourly-conversion) and [super and packaging information](/topics/super-and-packaging).
